rules.name: Prefetch data
rules.why: Windows Prefetch records that speed up app and boot launches. Windows rebuilds them, but boot and the first few app launches will be slower for a while.
sources: %SystemRoot%\Prefetch holds *.pf trace files that Windows regenerates automatically; deleting them only slows the next launches.

rules.name: Windows component store cleanup (DISM)
rules.why: Runs DISM StartComponentCleanup to remove superseded Windows update components from WinSxS. It never resets the base, so you keep the ability to uninstall updates. Can take a long time.
sources: DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /StartComponentCleanup is the supported way to reclaim WinSxS space. https://learn.microsoft.com/windows-hardware/manufacture/desktop/clean-up-the-winsxs-folder

rules.name: Clear Windows event logs
rules.why: Clears the Windows event logs. This frees a little space but erases troubleshooting history, so it is off by default.
sources: Event logs are cleared via the EventLog API; this is a standard administrative action that discards diagnostic history.

rules.name: Empty the Recycle Bin
rules.why: Permanently empties the Recycle Bin on all drives. This cannot be undone, so it is off by default and must be selected explicitly.
sources: SHEmptyRecycleBin is the documented API for emptying the Recycle Bin. https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/api/shellapi/nf-shellapi-shemptyrecyclebinw
